Notes is a room, and Pinned folds into it

One door in You, always drawn. Behind it a room on the standard chassis: the lead box, folders as kind tiles, two verb rows, then the rows — your jots and the things you pinned, in one list. Pin becomes the way anything in the app gets into Notes; the separate Pinned door and room go.

What changes in the rulings. Pinboard's own header deferred grouping as "one more field on these same rows, not a different shape" — that field is the folder, and it serves jots and pinned things alike. The Pinned door (§961) is deleted: its job was a list you built by hand, and that is now this room. The row verb keeps its word and glyph, Pin, and its confirmation says where it went ("Pinned to Notes"). Swipe-to-delete is a WRITE on a swipe, which the standing rule ("swipe verbs are reads only") forbids — this reverses it for this one room, where every row is yours: a jot's trailing swipe is Delete, a pinned thing's is Unpin (the thing stays in its source room, so nothing irreversible rides the gesture). delete-guard-audit.py covers the jot's delete.
The tile order, and why All leads. You were torn between New · Pinned · All · Folders and All first. The default is whichever tile is LIT, not whichever is first — and every room in the app lights All in the first slot, so a person who has learned one room has learned this one. New goes last for the same reason: a verb at the end of a scope row reads as a verb (it never lights, it is drawn in tint), and it is where the thumb lands on a right-handed phone. Four tiles, one row, no fifth. (Folders are flat: one level, a thing in one folder. A pinned thing keeps its own source mark, so the room reads as a shelf of your things, not a second feed.)
Reorder: declined, and what stands in for it. Pinboard's ruling stands — no ordering you maintain. Hand-ordered rows among time-ordered rooms is a second list grammar to learn, and the tool for "this one on top" already exists: Pin it (a jot pins like anything else, and Pinned is one tile away). Folders are the other hand-order. The room reads as one plain list with no day dividers (ruled: Apple Notes does not separate by day either), folders and Pin for the rest — not drag-to-reorder.
Apple Notes leaves the catalogue. Its seat was share-sheet instructions with nothing to read (§230a: "the tile that could never fill"), and Messages, Mail and Obsidian have no seat for being share destinations either. With a native Notes room, the seat is deleted from BridgeCatalog.offers, the website shelf and the marquees in the same session (the catalog-sync rule). Obsidian, Day One and Apple Journal stay: they IMPORT.
